full_judgment:
Shahidul Karim J: On an application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short, the Code), Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 18-7-2016 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Sessions Case No. 559 of 2016, arising out of GR No. 257 of 2013, corresponding to Savar Police Station Case No. 55 dated 25-04-2013, under sections 302/326/325/427/114/109/34 of the Penal Code should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. After lodgment of the case, police took up investigation of the same and having found prima-facie incriminating materials submitted charge-sheet being No.186 dated 24-05-2015 under sections 302/326/325/337/338/427/465/ 471/212/114/109/34 of the Penal Code against 41 (forty one) accused including the accused-petitioners. 

 7. While the case was pending in the said court, the accused-petitioners on 15.5-2016 filed an application under section 265C of the Code praying for discharge and the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka, upon taking hearing, rejected the same vide his order dated 18-7-2016 and framed charge against them including other accused under sections 302/326/325/427/114/109/34 of the Penal Code and set out the next date on 18-09-2016 for examination of witnesses. 

 9. Mr A SM Abdul Mobin, learned Advocate with Mr Sanjoy Kumar Kundu appearing for the accused-petitioners submits that the allegations brought against the accused-petitioners do not construe any offence under sections 302/326/ 325/427/114/109/34 of the Penal Code but the learned Sessions Judge without considering this vital aspect of the case most illegally framed charge against them by the impugned order. He further submits that admittedly the accused-petitioners are public servant and as per section 197(1) of the Code prior sanction of the government is a pre-requisite to start a criminal proceeding against them. But no such sanction has been obtained in the present case and in such view of the matter taking cognizance of the offences as well as framing charge against the accused-petitioners is wholly illegal and contrary to law and therefore, the impugned order is liable to be knocked down. 

 21. Whether the accused-petitioners acted or purported to act in discharge of their official duty is purely a question of fact to be decided on the basis of evidence at the trial.
